notes.dropped_milestones: none; all eight built unmodified with their pinned rustc 1.97.1
notes.exp032_commit_inference: exp-032 frontmatter has commit: null; its candidate is described as the final Rust-1.85-compatible code through exp-030. The only code commit between the first measurement (49629545) and the re-anchored record (0f9b946c, docs only) is c9c91d95, so c9c91d95 is used. The recorded exp-032 binary was a perf_probe, not the CLI.
notes.build_command: cd wt-<label> && CARGO_TARGET_DIR=<scratch>/targets/<label> cargo build --locked --release -p fdu --bin fdu (rustc 1.97.1 from each commit's rust-toolchain.toml); binary copied to bin/fdu-<label>
notes.invocation: prework and exp032 have no --cache flag and no .gitignore support: fdu --no-cache --color never ROOT (their default reads and writes a snapshot). v0.1.0 onward: fdu --cache off --color never ROOT (default tree view; .gitignore read by default; the tree has no ignore files). Cache-off was used for every version so no run could start from a snapshot written by an earlier one; v0.1.0 help lists its default --cache auto beside refresh/read-only/only, and v0.2.0+ describe auto as where it pays for this run. The harness also gave each process an isolated empty XDG_CACHE_HOME.
notes.answer_check: Before timing, every version run once under the harness environment: exit 0, root line 875,000 files, and exact JSON totals 875,000 files / 125,000 descendant dirs / 793,658,448 apparent / 2,986,741,760 allocated bytes / complete=true for all eight; nothing written to the isolated cache dir. See answer-check.tsv.
notes.harness_extension: benchmarks.realtree.compare_tools was run unmodified through drive_history.py, which registers two contracts (fdu-history-cache-off, fdu-history-no-cache) because no shipped contract is the default tree with the cache off. These contracts carry no per-sample semantic check; only exit status is checked per sample, hence the separate pre-timing answer check.
notes.storage_regime: Corpus on the external USB APFS SSD as briefed, not the internal SSD the 2026-09-26/28 report used. Every version from exp032 on spends about 42-44 s system CPU in about 30 s wall; the internal-SSD report measured about 37 s system CPU in 6.4 s wall. Inference: on this volume the wall is set by the kernel/USB I/O path, so post-campaign-1 engine work shows in user CPU and peak RSS, not wall. Absolute seconds are not comparable with the report.
notes.host: Uncontrolled: CPU busy 22-96% (median 38.6%) at sample boundaries, 96% above the 25% quiet gate; load 6-19. Declared host_regime uncontrolled and stage exploratory (the Makefile defaults); the gate was not altered. Four non-pre-work samples above 45 s (54-109 s) coincide with 79-94% CPU busy; they are valid under the regime and remain in the medians.
notes.release_qualification_table: The rendered report's release-qualification column is the harness's resource-limit classification for held-out release claims; it does not apply to this exploratory cell.
notes.v0_1_0_stdout: v0.1.0 prints a Performance line with the elapsed time on stdout, so its 12 stdout hashes differ; every other version printed one stable stdout.
